passages.text: Now for the matters you wrote about: It is good to abstain from sexual relations.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Corinth.
Paul answered questions from the church.
Paul said, “It is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman.”
Paul taught that abstaining from sexual relations is good.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ ὧν ἐγράψατε καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ γυναικὸς μὴ ἅπτεσθαι

passages.text: But because there is so much sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
passages.sermon: There is much sexual immorality in the world.\r\nEach man should have his own wife.\r\nEach woman should have her own husband.
passages.original: διὰ δὲ τὰς πορνείας ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα ἐχέτω καὶ ἑκάστη τὸν ἴδιον ἄνδρα ἐχέτω

passages.text: The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband.
passages.sermon: A husband should fulfill his duty to his wife.\r\nA wife should fulfill her duty to her husband.
passages.original: Τῇ γυναικὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἀποδιδότω ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ τῷ ἀνδρί

passages.text: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband. Likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.
passages.sermon:
A wife does not have authority over her own body.
Her husband has authority over her body.
A husband does not have authority over his own body.
His wife has authority over his body.
passages.original: ἡ γυνὴ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλὰ ὁ ἀνήρ ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλὰ ἡ γυνή

passages.text: Do not deprive each other, except by mutual consent and for a time, so you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan will not tempt you through your lack of self-control.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christian husbands and wives.
He tells them not to deprive each other.
They may separate only if both agree.
They may separate only for a short time.
They may separate so they can devote themselves to prayer.
After this time, they should come together again.
If they do not come together, Satan may tempt them.
Satan tempts them because of their lack of self-control.
passages.original: Μὴ ἀποστερεῖτε ἀλλήλους εἰ μήτι ἂν ἐκ συμφώνου πρὸς καιρὸν ἵνα σχολάσητε τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ πάλιν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἦτε ἵνα μὴ πειράζῃ ὑμᾶς ὁ Σατανᾶς διὰ τὴν ἀκρασίαν ὑμῶν

passages.text: I say this as a concession, not as a command.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul gives advice about marriage and self-control.
Paul says, “I say this as a concession.”
Paul does not give a command.
Paul allows this as permission, not as a rule.
passages.original: τοῦτο δὲ λέγω κατὰ συνγνώμην οὐ κατ’ ἐπιταγήν

passages.text: I wish that all men were as I am. But each man has his own gift from God; one has this gift, another has that.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul wishes that all people could be like him.
Paul is unmarried and devoted to God.
But God gives each person a different gift.
One person receives one kind of gift from God.
Another person receives a different gift from God.
passages.original: θέλω δὲ πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἶναι ὡς καὶ ἐμαυτόν ἀλλὰ ἕκαστος ἴδιον ἔχει χάρισμα ἐκ Θεοῦ ὁ μὲν οὕτως ὁ δὲ οὕτως

passages.text: Now to the unmarried and widows I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the unmarried and to widows.
Paul is unmarried.
Paul says it is good for the unmarried and widows to remain unmarried.
Paul says they should remain as he is.
passages.original: Λέγω δὲ τοῖς ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς χήραις καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγώ

passages.text: But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn with passion.
passages.sermon: Some people cannot control themselves.\r\nThese people should marry.\r\nIt is better to marry than to burn with passion.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἐγκρατεύονται γαμησάτωσαν κρεῖττον γάρ ἐστιν γαμῆσαι ἢ πυροῦσθαι

passages.text: To the married I give this command (not I, but the Lord): A wife must not separate from her husband.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to married people.
Paul gives a command.
This command comes from the Lord, not from Paul himself.
A wife must not separate from her husband.
passages.original: Τοῖς δὲ γεγαμηκόσιν παραγγέλλω οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλὰ ὁ Κύριος γυναῖκα ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς μὴ χωρισθῆναι

passages.text: But if she does, she must remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
passages.sermon:
A married woman must not separate from her husband.
If she separates, she must stay unmarried.
Or she must be reconciled to her husband.
A husband must not divorce his wife.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ χωρισθῇ μενέτω ἄγαμος ἢ τῷ ἀνδρὶ καταλλαγήτω καὶ ἄνδρα γυναῖκα μὴ ἀφιέναι

passages.text: To the rest I say this (I, not the Lord): If a brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing to live with him, he must not divorce her.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the rest of the believers.
Paul, not the Lord, gives this instruction.
A Christian man may have a wife who does not believe in Christ.
If this unbelieving wife agrees to live with him,
The Christian husband must not divorce her.
passages.original: Τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς λέγω ἐγώ οὐχ ὁ Κύριος εἴ τις ἀδελφὸς γυναῖκα ἔχει ἄπιστον καὶ αὕτη συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετ’ αὐτοῦ μὴ ἀφιέτω αὐτήν

passages.text: And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.
passages.sermon: A woman may have a husband who does not believe in Christ.\r\nThis husband may be willing to live with her.\r\nIf he is willing to live with her, she must not divorce him.
passages.original: καὶ γυνὴ εἴ τις ἔχει ἄνδρα ἄπιστον καὶ οὗτος συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετ’ αὐτῆς μὴ ἀφιέτω τὸν ἄνδρα

passages.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through her believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
passages.sermon:
A believing spouse can sanctify an unbelieving spouse.
A believing wife sanctifies her unbelieving husband.
A believing husband sanctifies his unbelieving wife.
If this were not true, your children would be unclean.
But now your children are holy.
passages.original: ἡγίασται γὰρ ὁ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἄπιστος ἐν τῇ γυναικί καὶ ἡγίασται ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ἄπιστος ἐν τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἐπεὶ ἄρα τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν ἀκάθαρτά ἐστιν νῦν δὲ ἅγιά ἐστιν

passages.text: But if the unbeliever leaves, let him go. The believing brother or sister is not bound in such cases. God has called you to live in peace.
passages.sermon: If the unbelieving spouse chooses to leave, let that person leave.\r\nThe believing husband or wife is not bound in these situations.\r\nGod has called you to live in peace.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ὁ ἄπιστος χωρίζεται χωριζέσθω οὐ δεδούλωται ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἡ ἀδελφὴ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις ἐν δὲ εἰρήνῃ κέκληκεν ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεός

passages.text: How do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
passages.sermon:
A wife may have an unbelieving husband.
A husband may have an unbelieving wife.
Wife, you do not know if you will save your husband.
Husband, you do not know if you will save your wife.
passages.original: τί γὰρ οἶδας γύναι εἰ τὸν ἄνδρα σώσεις ἢ τί οἶδας ἄνερ εἰ τὴν γυναῖκα σώσεις

passages.text: Regardless, each one should lead the life that the Lord has assigned to him and to which God has called him. This is what I prescribe in all the churches.
passages.sermon:
God calls each person to a certain life.
The Lord assigns each person a place and purpose.
Each person should live as God has called them.
I give this instruction to every church.
passages.original: Εἰ μὴ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ἐμέρισεν ὁ Κύριος ἕκαστον ὡς κέκληκεν ὁ Θεός οὕτως περιπατείτω καὶ οὕτως ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις πάσαις διατάσσομαι

passages.text: Was a man already circumcised when he was called? He should not become uncircumcised. Was a man still uncircumcised when called? He should not be circumcised.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote to the church in Corinth.
He taught about how to live as a Christian.
He said, “If God called a man when he was already circumcised, he should not try to become uncircumcised.”
“If God called a man when he was not circumcised, he should not get circumcised.”
passages.original: περιτετμημένος τις ἐκλήθη μὴ ἐπισπάσθω ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ κέκληταί τις μὴ περιτεμνέσθω

passages.text: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing. Keeping God’s commandments is what counts.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in the church.
Paul says circumcision does not matter.
Paul says uncircumcision does not matter.
Obeying God’s commandments is what matters.
passages.original: ἡ περιτομὴ οὐδέν ἐστιν καὶ ἡ ἀκροβυστία οὐδέν ἐστιν ἀλλὰ τήρησις ἐντολῶν Θεοῦ

passages.text: Each one should remain in the situation he was in when he was called.
passages.sermon: Paul wrote to the Christians in Corinth.\r\nPaul taught about following Jesus.\r\nPaul said, “Each person should stay in the situation he was in when God called him.”
passages.original: Ἕκαστος ἐν τῇ κλήσει ᾗ ἐκλήθη ἐν ταύτῃ μενέτω

passages.text: Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it concern you—but if you can gain your freedom, take the opportunity.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians who were slaves when God called them.
He says, “Were you a slave when God called you?”
Do not let this trouble you.
If you can become free, use that chance.
Take the opportunity to gain your freedom.
passages.original: δοῦλος ἐκλήθης μή σοι μελέτω ἀλλ’ εἰ καὶ δύνασαι ἐλεύθερος γενέσθαι μᾶλλον χρῆσαι

passages.text: For he who was a slave when he was called by the Lord is the Lord’s freedman. Conversely, he who was a free man when he was called is Christ’s slave.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians about their status when God called them.
Some Christians were slaves when the Lord called them.
God called these slaves to follow Him.
The Lord makes these slaves free in Him.
Some Christians were free when God called them.
God called these free people to follow Christ.
These free people become slaves of Christ.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐν Κυρίῳ κληθεὶς δοῦλος ἀπελεύθερος Κυρίου ἐστίν ὁμοίως ὁ ἐλεύθερος κληθεὶς δοῦλός ἐστιν Χριστοῦ

passages.text: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of men.
passages.sermon: God bought you at a price.\r\nDo not become slaves of people.
passages.original: Τιμῆς ἠγοράσθητε μὴ γίνεσθε δοῦλοι ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: Brothers, each one should remain in the situation he was in when God called him.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christian brothers.
God called each person in a certain situation.
Each person should stay in the situation where God called him.
Stay with God in that situation.
passages.original: ἕκαστος ἐν ᾧ ἐκλήθη ἀδελφοί ἐν τούτῳ μενέτω παρὰ Θεῷ

passages.text: Now about virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul addresses the topic of virgins.
Paul says he has no command from the Lord about this.
Paul gives his own judgment on the matter.
Paul says the Lord has shown him mercy.
Paul says he is trustworthy because of the Lord’s mercy.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν παρθένων ἐπιταγὴν Κυρίου οὐκ ἔχω γνώμην δὲ δίδωμι ὡς ἠλεημένος ὑπὸ Κυρίου πιστὸς εἶναι

passages.text: Because of the present crisis, I think it is good for a man to remain as he is.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul is an apostle and a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul is trustworthy by the Lord’s mercy.
There is a present crisis.
Because of this crisis, Paul gives advice.
Paul thinks it is good for a man to remain as he is.
passages.original: Νομίζω οὖν τοῦτο καλὸν ὑπάρχειν διὰ τὴν ἐνεστῶσαν ἀνάγκην ὅτι καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ οὕτως εἶναι

passages.text: Are you committed to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free of commitment? Do not look for a wife.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to Christians in Corinth.
Paul is giving advice about marriage.
Paul is trustworthy because the Lord has shown him mercy.
Are you married to a wife?
Do not try to end your marriage.
Are you not married?
Do not look for a wife.
passages.original: δέδεσαι γυναικί μὴ ζήτει λύσιν λέλυσαι ἀπὸ γυναικός μὴ ζήτει γυναῖκα

passages.text: But if you do marry, you have not sinned. And if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. But those who marry will face troubles in this life, and I want to spare you this.
passages.sermon:
If you marry, you do not sin.
If a virgin marries, she does not sin.
Those who marry will have troubles in this life.
I want to spare you from these troubles.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ γαμήσῃς οὐχ ἥμαρτες καὶ ἐὰν γήμῃ ἡ παρθένος οὐχ ἥμαρτεν θλῖψιν δὲ τῇ σαρκὶ ἕξουσιν οἱ τοιοῦτοι ἐγὼ δὲ ὑμῶν φείδομαι

passages.text: What I am saying, brothers, is that the time is short. From now on those who have wives should live as if they had none; those who weep, as if they did not; those who are joyful, as if they were not; those who make a purchase, as if they had nothing; and those who use the things of this world, as if not dependent on them. For this world in its present form is passing away.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the Christian brothers.
Paul says the time is short.
The present world is passing away.
Those who have wives should live as if they do not have wives.
Those who weep should live as if they do not weep.
Those who rejoice should live as if they do not rejoice.
Those who buy things should live as if they do not own them.
Those who use the things of this world should live as if they are not attached to them.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δέ φημι ἀδελφοί ὁ καιρὸς συνεσταλμένος ἐστίν τὸ λοιπὸν ἵνα καὶ οἱ ἔχοντες γυναῖκας ὡς μὴ ἔχοντες ὦσιν καὶ οἱ κλαίοντες ὡς μὴ κλαίοντες καὶ οἱ χαίροντες ὡς μὴ χαίροντες καὶ οἱ ἀγοράζοντες ὡς μὴ κατέχοντες καὶ οἱ χρώμενοι τὸν κόσμον ὡς μὴ καταχρώμενοι παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου

passages.text: I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the work of the Lord, how he can please the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church.
Paul wants the believers to be free from worry.
An unmarried man thinks about the Lord's work.
He wants to please the Lord.
passages.original: Θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους εἶναι ὁ ἄγαμος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ Κυρίου πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῷ Κυρίῳ

passages.text: But the married man is concerned about the affairs of this world, how he can please his wife, and his interests are divided. The unmarried woman or virgin is concerned about the work of the Lord, how she can be holy in both body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about the affairs of this world, how she can please her husband.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians about marriage and devotion to the Lord.
A married man thinks about the things of this world.
He tries to please his wife.
His attention is divided.
An unmarried woman or a virgin thinks about the work of the Lord.
She wants to be holy in her body.
She wants to be holy in her spirit.
A married woman thinks about the things of this world.
She tries to please her husband.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ γαμήσας μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῇ γυναικί καὶ μεμέρισται καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ἄγαμος καὶ ἡ παρθένος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ τῷ σώματι καὶ τῷ πνεύματι ἡ δὲ γαμήσασα μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῷ ἀνδρί

passages.text: I am saying this for your own good, not to restrict you, but in order to promote proper decorum and undivided devotion to the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul wants what is good for you.
Paul says this for your benefit.
Paul does not want to restrict you.
Paul does not want to put a burden on you.
Paul wants you to live properly.
Paul wants you to serve the Lord.
Paul wants you to be devoted to the Lord.
Paul wants you to give your full attention to the Lord.
Paul wants you to serve the Lord without distraction.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ πρὸς τὸ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν σύμφορον λέγω οὐχ ἵνα βρόχον ὑμῖν ἐπιβάλω ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὸ εὔσχημον καὶ εὐπάρεδρον τῷ Κυρίῳ ἀπερισπάστως

passages.text: However, if someone thinks he is acting inappropriately toward his betrothed, and if she is beyond her youth and they ought to marry, let him do as he wishes; he is not sinning; they should get married.
passages.sermon:
A man may have a woman promised to him in marriage.
He may think he is acting improperly toward her.
She may be past the age of marriage.
They may feel they ought to marry.
He may do what he wants.
He does not sin if he marries her.
They should get married.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τις ἀσχημονεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν παρθένον αὐτοῦ νομίζει ἐὰν ᾖ ὑπέρακμος καὶ οὕτως ὀφείλει γίνεσθαι ὃ θέλει ποιείτω οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει γαμείτωσαν

passages.text: But the man who is firmly established in his heart and under no constraint, with control over his will and resolve in his heart not to marry the virgin, he will do well.
passages.sermon:
A man may have a betrothed woman.
He may feel no pressure to marry her.
He may stand firm in his own heart.
He may have full control over his own will.
He may decide in his heart to keep his betrothed unmarried.
If he does this, he does well.
passages.original: ὃς δὲ ἕστηκεν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἑδραῖος μὴ ἔχων ἀνάγκην ἐξουσίαν δὲ ἔχει περὶ τοῦ ἰδίου θελήματος καὶ τοῦτο κέκρικεν ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ καρδίᾳ τηρεῖν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ παρθένον καλῶς ποιήσει

passages.text: So then, he who marries the virgin does well, but he who does not marry her does even better.
passages.sermon: A man may have a woman who is a virgin and is considering marriage.\r\nIf he marries her, he does well.\r\nIf he does not marry her, he does even better.
passages.original: Ὥστε καὶ ὁ γαμίζων τὴν ἑαυτοῦ παρθένον καλῶς ποιεῖ καὶ ὁ μὴ γαμίζων κρεῖσσον ποιήσει

passages.text: A wife is bound to her husband as long as he lives. But if her husband dies, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, as long as he belongs to the Lord.
passages.sermon:
A wife stays joined to her husband while he lives.
If her husband dies, she becomes free.
She may marry anyone she chooses.
She must marry only someone who belongs to the Lord.
passages.original: Γυνὴ δέδεται ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς ἐὰν δὲ κοιμηθῇ ὁ ἀνήρ ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ᾧ θέλει γαμηθῆναι μόνον ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: In my judgment, however, she is happier if she remains as she is. And I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking as an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Paul gives his personal judgment.
Paul says a widow is happier if she remains unmarried.
Paul believes he also has the Spirit of God.
passages.original: μακαριωτέρα δέ ἐστιν ἐὰν οὕτως μείνῃ κατὰ τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην δοκῶ δὲ κἀγὼ Πνεῦμα Θεοῦ ἔχειν
